title: Fictional community-kitchen shift coordination
provenance: All people, statements and scenarios below are synthetic benchmark fixtures, not customer evidence.

analysis.decisionQuestion: What should a volunteer shift coordination pilot solve without confusing privacy, access and approval preferences?
questions: Which recurring needs are supported across these selected fictional interviews? Distinguish synthesis from merely repeating quotations.
Which preferences genuinely conflict, and which can coexist? Explain the source-backed distinction without inventing a conflict.
What decision-critical evidence is missing, and what should be tested before committing to requirements?

turns.speaker: anita
turns.text: Three versions of the rota circulate in messages. I need one current rota and an explicit confirmation when someone accepts a shift.

turns.speaker: anita
turns.text: Every shift swap must wait for coordinator approval before the replacement becomes responsible, including swaps between two trained volunteers.

turns.speaker: anita
turns.text: I do not have a measured no-show rate. Nobody has agreed a retention target or an operating budget for a new system.

turns.speaker: berit
turns.text: I once followed an old rota and arrived on the wrong day. Show which version is current and tell me that my shift acceptance was recorded.

turns.speaker: berit
turns.text: A swap between two trained volunteers must become effective as soon as both accept, without waiting for any coordinator approval. The coordinator can be notified afterwards.

turns.speaker: berit
turns.text: I prefer text-message reminders because I do not want to install an app. I am happy to open a rota link in my phone's browser.

turns.speaker: cem
turns.text: I want to see my confirmed shifts and which named teammate is on duty, without hunting through the chat.

turns.speaker: cem
turns.text: Showing a teammate's first name on the rota is fine. Do not publish everyone's phone number to the whole volunteer group. I have no preference about swap approval.

turns.speaker: cem
turns.text: Nobody asked me to test accessibility or language options. Please do not assume that every volunteer has a smartphone.

turns.speaker: daria
turns.text: We need a single current rota with a clear accepted-or-unconfirmed status for each assignment. I also need to see whether someone is trained for the kitchen task.

turns.speaker: daria
turns.text: A phone browser and text-message reminders are enough for a first pilot; we do not need a native app. Do not put donor fundraising or meal stock management into this pilot.

turns.speaker: daria
turns.text: We could test for three weeks in this kitchen. We have not checked text-message costs, consent requirements or who maintains training records. These conversations did not include volunteers without phones.

prdBrief: Create a concise product PRD for a three-week, one-kitchen volunteer rota pilot from the selected synthetic interview analysis. Include recurring needs, genuine tensions versus compatible preferences, source-linked prioritized requirements, testable acceptance checks, proposed metrics and a measurement plan, non-goals, unknowns and next steps. Do not turn fictional statements into real customer evidence. Preserve the unresolved swap-approval decision and account for missing accessibility and non-phone-user evidence. Any numerical success threshold or owner not explicitly supplied is a proposal, not an agreed fact.

reviewCriteria.expected: Synthesizes a common need for one authoritative rota plus explicit assignment acceptance from Anita, Berit, Cem or Daria, rather than only listing separate quotes.
Identifies mandatory coordinator approval before every swap versus immediate swaps between trained volunteers as a genuine policy conflict; does not quietly choose a winner.
Recognizes text-message reminders and browser access are compatible, and neither requires installing a native app.
Recognizes displaying first names on the rota is compatible with withholding group-wide phone numbers; does not manufacture an anonymity-versus-coordination conflict.
Notes missing no-show baseline, budget/SMS costs/consent, training-record ownership, accessibility/language and non-phone-user evidence; avoids inventing outcomes or universal smartphone access.
Keeps a one-kitchen/three-week scenario pilot, with fundraising, meal inventory and native app development excluded or explicitly deferred.
Gives observable checks for current rota consistency, recorded acceptance, training suitability and phone-number access control; handles swap approval as a testable proposal or unresolved decision.

Proposes baseline and pilot comparisons for rota confusion or unconfirmed shifts, and recruitment/testing to cover absent non-phone/accessibility perspectives. Numerical success targets remain proposals.
Key analytical claims and requirements have followable supporting sources/finding IDs, not decorative unrelated citations.
Preserves fictional/synthetic provenance and does not assert real customer validation, population prevalence, invented quotations or verified facts.
